citation: Nemhauser, Wolsey, Fisher (1978). An analysis of approximations for maximizing submodular set functions - I
problem: Cardinality-constrained maximization of monotone submodular set functions
method: Worst-case analysis of greedy and interchange heuristics; (1-1/e) approximation guarantee for greedy under monotone submodularity
closest overlap with our work: Canonical justification for greedy/fixed-ranking placement: greedy is near-optimal only when the objective is monotone submodular
exact remaining gap: Guarantee is void when the objective is neither submodular nor supermodular (our alpha(S) has discrete second differences of both signs); says nothing about small-signal stability margins

citation: Topkis (1978). Minimizing a submodular function on a lattice
problem: Conditions under which optimal solutions of parametric problems are monotone (isotone) in the parameter; submodular minimization on lattices
method: Lattice-theoretic analysis; increasing differences / submodularity implies monotone comparative statics
closest overlap with our work: Explains when a fixed (context-free) ordering of choices can be optimal (consistent-sign differences); our sign-mixed second differences violate this premise
exact remaining gap: No dynamic-system or stability application

citation: Lovász (1983). Submodular functions and convexity
venue: In: Mathematical Programming The State of the Art, Springer Berlin Heidelberg, pp. 235-257
problem: Structural link between submodular set functions and convex functions
method: Lovász extension: a set function is submodular iff its extension is convex; polyhedral characterization
closest overlap with our work: Provides the formal definition/test (non-positive vs non-negative second differences) we apply to alpha(S)
exact remaining gap: Pure theory; no power-system or eigenvalue objective

citation: Smed (1993). Feasible eigenvalue sensitivity for large power systems

method: First-order eigenvalue sensitivity derived on the sparse (augmented DAE) formulation; effect of control actions (e.g., P/Q modulation) from one eigen-solution; HVDC damping design example
closest overlap with our work: Foundational sparse eigenvalue sensitivity that underlies computing dlambda/da on the augmented (network-explicit) model
exact remaining gap: Sensitivity to control actions only; no branch-admittance total derivative with re-solved power flow; no ranking validation against finite interventions; synchronous-machine era

citation: Topkis (1998). Supermodularity and complementarity
venue: Princeton University Press (Frontiers of Economic Research)
problem: Theory of supermodularity, complementarity and monotone comparative statics
method: Book-length treatment of supermodular functions on lattices, increasing differences, and monotone optimal solutions
closest overlap with our work: Standard reference for complementarity (supermodular) vs substitutability (submodular) between elements; our SG->GFL replacements act as complements in some contexts and substitutes in others
exact remaining gap: No power-system content

citation: Nam, Kim, Shim et al. (2000). A new eigen-sensitivity theory of augmented matrix and its applications to power system stability analysis
problem: First- and second-order eigenvalue sensitivity/perturbation of the augmented matrix for small-signal and voltage stability

closest overlap with our work: Same IEEE 39-bus; computes eigenvalue sensitivity to line reactance and ranks lines; compares frozen-operating-point estimates with load-flow-re-solved recomputation (voltage-stability part) and reports that line rankings differ from branch participation factor and change between base and critical loading
exact remaining gap: Oscillatory-mode line sensitivities are partial (re-solution not stated); no total IFT derivative; no GFL converters or replacement portfolios; no rank-correlation test against finite reinforcements or against graph metrics (Fiedler, Kirchhoff, gSCR)

citation: Coletta, Jacquod (2016). Linear stability and the Braess paradox in coupled-oscillator networks and electric power grids

citation: Mendoza-Armenta, Dobson (2016). Applying a formula for generator redispatch to damp interarea oscillations using synchrophasors
problem: Rank generator pairs for redispatch to damp a poorly damped interarea mode

closest overlap with our work: Explicit operating-point-induced (re-equilibrated) eigenvalue sensitivity; the formula decomposes the effect line by line through angle changes across lines and ranks candidate actions
exact remaining gap: Parameter is dispatch, not branch admittance; lossless lines and constant internal voltages (swing-equation generators); no converters, no nested portfolios, no comparison with frozen partial or static topology metrics

citation: Summers, Cortesi, Lygeros (2016). On submodularity and controllability in complex dynamical networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems 3(1):91-101 (Corrections: TCNS 5(3):1503, 2018, doi 10.1109/TCNS.2017.2670506)

closest overlap with our work: Closest control-theory precedent for treating a placement set function on a linear dynamical network; power-grid example
exact remaining gap: Metrics are Gramian energy measures of a fixed linear model, not the rightmost eigenvalue of a re-linearized system after re-solving equilibrium; no SG->GFL replacement, no sign reversal of marginal effects; the correction shows submodularity claims are fragile

citation: Khaji, Aghamohammadi (2017). Emergency transmission line switching to suppress power system inter-area oscillation
venue: International Journal of Electrical Power & Energy Systems
problem: Emergency damping control of interarea oscillations by line switching
method: Off-line sensitivity of interarea damping ratio with respect to each line switching used as a priority list; WAMS-based brittleness index for timing
closest overlap with our work: Ranks lines by their effect on interarea damping (line switching as damping control)
exact remaining gap: Relies on a precomputed (fixed) priority list, which is exactly the type of fixed ranking we show can fail across contexts; no IBRs; no total sensitivity or static-metric comparison

citation: Li, Qi, Wang et al. (2017). An SQP method combined with gradient sampling for small-signal stability constrained OPF
problem: Small-signal-stability-constrained OPF with nonsmooth spectral abscissa
method: SQP with gradient sampling; closed-form first-order eigenvalue sensitivities d(lambda)/dx = psi (dA/dx) phi / psi phi with dA/dx via the DAE blocks (A~,B~,C~,D~); power-flow equations kept as OPF equality constraints so every iterate is a re-solved equilibrium
closest overlap with our work: Uses eigenvalue sensitivity through the DAE (algebraic network) blocks inside an optimization that re-solves the equilibrium; spectral abscissa is the rightmost-eigenvalue metric we also track
exact remaining gap: Decision variables are dispatch/voltages, not network admittances; no topology, no IBRs; no assessment of how well sensitivities rank finite interventions

citation: Ebrahimzadeh, Blaabjerg, Wang, et al. (2018). Bus Participation Factor Analysis for Harmonic Instability in Power Electronics Based Power Systems
problem: Locate which converters and buses are most sensitive to and contribute most to harmonic instability.

closest overlap with our work: Node/bus criticality defined via mode sensitivity for converter-driven oscillations.
exact remaining gap: Harmonic (high-frequency) instability inside a wind farm, not 0.1-2 Hz electromechanical modes; no replacement portfolios, sign reversal, or line ranking vs finite interventions.

citation: Li, Chiang, Du (2018). Online line switching method for enhancing the small-signal stability margin of power systems
problem: Line switching to increase small-signal stability margin when injections shift
method: Three-stage online method: screening, ranking, detailed evaluation of candidate line switchings; IEEE test systems
closest overlap with our work: Topology action ranked for small-signal margin with operating-point-dependent need
exact remaining gap: Synchronous-machine systems; ranking accuracy vs finite re-solved outcomes and static metrics not reported in abstract; no GFL portfolios

citation: Olshevsky (2018). On (non)supermodularity of average control energy
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems 5(3):1177-1181
problem: Whether average control energy (trace of inverse Gramian) is supermodular in the actuated set
method: Proof that the function is not necessarily supermodular, correcting prior literature
closest overlap with our work: Precedent that natural dynamic performance set functions can fail modularity assumptions; supports our non-sub/non-supermodularity finding
exact remaining gap: Energy metric, not an eigenvalue stability margin; no power-system equilibrium re-solution, no IBR replacement, no quantification of greedy/fixed-ranking failure rates

citation: Song, Hill, Liu (2018). Network-Based Analysis of Small-Disturbance Angle Stability of Power Systems
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems 5(3):901-912
problem: Role of network topology in small-disturbance angle stability; mechanism of instability.
method: Active power flow graph whose Laplacian weights depend on operating angles (negative weights = critical lines); inertia of that Laplacian determines stability/type of equilibrium; necessary-and-sufficient criterion via critical-line matrix; equivalent weight ('electrical antagonism') as stability index.
closest overlap with our work: Operating-point-dependent graph Laplacian in which a line's contribution can change sign (critical lines). This is the structural analogue of the contextual sign reversal we find.
exact remaining gap: Classical SG swing-equation model with no converters or GFL; the sign change is of an edge weight with operating angle, not of a generator replacement's marginal effect across portfolios. No ranking validation against finite interventions.

citation: Wu, Li, Javadi, et al. (2018). Assessing Impact of Renewable Energy Integration on System Strength Using Site-Dependent Short Circuit Ratio
problem: Existing SCR-based strength indices ignore electrical interactions among multiple renewable sites.
method: Site-dependent SCR (SDSCR) derived from the relationship between system strength and voltage stability; IEEE 39-bus case studies.
closest overlap with our work: Site-dependent (node) strength metric on the IEEE 39-bus system; the kind of static node metric we benchmark against.
exact remaining gap: Static voltage-stability index; no small-signal eigenvalue, no replacement portfolios or sign analysis, no line ranking validated against finite reinforcements.

citation: Dong, Xin, Wu, et al. (2019). Small Signal Stability Analysis of Multi-Infeed Power Electronic Systems Based on Grid Strength Assessment
problem: Relate small-signal stability of multi-infeed power-electronic systems to grid strength; generalize SCR/CSCR to multi-infeed (gSCR, CgSCR).
method: Analytical SCR-stability relation for single infeed; extension by eigenvalue decomposition (modal decoupling) of the capacity-weighted Kron-reduced network matrix under homogeneous devices; checked by eigenvalue analysis and time-domain simulation.
closest overlap with our work: Defines gSCR, one of our static baselines; the smallest eigenvalue of the weighted network matrix sets the PLL-band margin.
exact remaining gap: Single system-level index at rated conditions with homogeneous GFL devices and no synchronous-machine electromechanical modes; does not compute per-replacement marginal effects, sign changes across portfolios, or line-reinforcement rankings checked against finite interventions.

citation: Li, Li, Shi et al. (2019). An efficient numerical method for computing eigenvalue sensitivity with respect to operational parameters of large-scale power systems

closest overlap with our work: Explicitly includes operating-point change (perturbed power flow) in eigenvalue sensitivity - the re-equilibration ingredient of our total sensitivity
exact remaining gap: Operational (injection/voltage) parameters only; no branch admittance, no analytic IFT form, no IBR portfolios, no ranking validation against finite interventions or static metrics

citation: Liu, Clark, Bushnell et al. (2019). Controlled islanding via weak submodularity

closest overlap with our work: TPWRS precedent for using weak submodularity (submodularity ratio) on IEEE 39-bus set-selection problems

citation: Poolla, Groß, Dörfler (2019). Placement and implementation of grid-forming and grid-following virtual inertia and fast frequency response
problem: Optimal location and tuning of GFM and GFL virtual inertia/fast frequency response devices

closest overlap with our work: Placement of GFM vs GFL devices; optimal allocation depends on implementation (GFM vs GFL)

citation: Qin, Yang, Rajagopal (2019). Submodularity of storage placement optimization in power networks

citation: Markovic, Stanojev, Aristidou, et al. (2021). Understanding Small-Signal Stability of Low-Inertia Systems
problem: Stability properties of low-inertia systems with SGs, GFM and GFL converters; maximum permissible IBR penetration.
method: High-fidelity full-order model incl. line and load dynamics; modal analysis, participation factors, parameter sensitivity; nature of unstable modes; directions for improving margins under different generation portfolios on several benchmark systems.
closest overlap with our work: Replaces SGs with converter-based generation across generation portfolios and uses participation factors to find vulnerable segments; closest system-level precursor to (i).
exact remaining gap: Per the abstract, results are organized by penetration level and portfolio type. citation: Yang, Huang, Xin, et al. (2021). Placing Grid-Forming Converters to Enhance Small Signal Stability of PLL-Integrated Power Systems
problem: Where to convert PLL-based converters to grid-forming control to best improve PLL-band small-signal stability.
method: Matrix perturbation theory shows GFM placement is equivalent to increasing gSCR. Placement maximizes the smallest eigenvalue of the capacity-weighted Kron-reduced Laplacian with GFM rows/columns deleted (combinatorial). A greedy heuristic recomputes node participation factors on the smallest eigenvalue after each placement. Two-area and modified 39-bus systems.
closest overlap with our work: Closest to (i)-(ii): subset selection of converter conversions on a 39-bus system, node participation ranking on a Laplacian eigenvalue, and sequential (context-updated) greedy selection; the authors note greedy is not guaranteed optimal.
exact remaining gap: Under their homogeneous-PLL, static-Laplacian model with no SG dynamics, Proposition III.4 (interlacing) makes every PLL-to-GFM conversion stabilizing, so sign reversal is impossible by construction. They do not quantify fixed-ranking failure rates across stable contexts and do not use re-equilibrated full-system eigenvalue sensitivities.

citation: Huang, Xin, Dong, et al. (2022). Impacts of Grid Structure on PLL-Synchronization Stability of Converter-Integrated Power Systems
problem: How grid structure affects PLL-synchronization stability of multi-converter systems.
method: Kron reduction to converter nodes; modal decoupling (homogeneous converters, uniform R/L, constant-current loads, infinite bus); smallest eigenvalue of the grounded Kron-reduced Laplacian sets the margin; closed-form sensitivity of that eigenvalue to line susceptance B_ij (effective-resistance form); guidelines on PLL retuning, converter placement, reinforcing weak connections; 39-bus.
closest overlap with our work: Closest peer-reviewed precursor of (iii): line-level sensitivity used to choose which weak connection to reinforce for converter small-signal margin, on a 39-bus network.
exact remaining gap: The sensitivity is of a static network eigenvalue, not the re-equilibrated (implicit-function) total derivative of the full-system rightmost eigenvalue. The model has no SGs or electromechanical modes, and the smallest eigenvalue is stated to be monotone in network connectivity (reinforcement never hurts). Rankings are not scored against finite reinforcements or against alternative static metrics.

citation: Schafer, Pesch, Manik, et al. (2022). Understanding Braess' Paradox in power grids
problem: Adding lines or increasing line capacity can reduce grid performance (Braess' paradox) in realistic grids.
method: Experimental AC grid demonstration plus a topological (flow/cycle-based) theory predicting Braessian edges from network structure; implications for grid-extension planning.
closest overlap with our work: Shows the sign of a link reinforcement's effect depends on the network/flow context, which motivates scoring finite reinforcements rather than assuming monotone benefit.
exact remaining gap: Steady-state line loading, not small-signal eigenvalues or IBR/GFL dynamics; no generator replacement portfolios, no eigenvalue-sensitivity ranking or static-metric comparison for small-signal stability.

citation: Zhu, Gu, Li, et al. (2022). Participation Analysis in Impedance Models: The Grey-Box Approach for Power System Stability
problem: Root-cause tracing of small-signal instability without full disclosure of IBR internal models.
method: Impedance participation factor defined as the residue of the whole-system admittance matrix and proved equal to the eigenvalue sensitivity with respect to apparatus impedance; chain rule to state and parameter participation; three-layer grey-box approach.
closest overlap with our work: Apparatus-level eigenvalue sensitivity as a criticality measure; conceptual parent of node-level eigenvalue-sensitivity rankings.
exact remaining gap: First-order local sensitivity at a fixed operating point and portfolio (apparatus impedances not re-equilibrated). It does not study discrete SG-to-GFL replacements, sign changes of their effect across portfolios, or whether any fixed ranking selects the best next replacement.

citation: Gu, Green (2023). Power System Stability With a High Penetration of Inverter-Based Resources
problem: How IBR dynamics fit or break classical stability categories; GFL vs GFM synchronization, inertia and voltage strength.
method: Review and analysis; GFL/GFM duality and generalized angle dynamics; discussion of system strength and GFM placement; research agenda.
closest overlap with our work: Calls for spatial-temporal indices of system strength and stability margin to guide where new stability services go. Our portfolio-conditioned indices address this agenda item.
exact remaining gap: Review. No quantitative portfolio-conditioned marginal analysis, no sign-reversal evidence, no ranking evaluation against finite interventions.

citation: Li, Green, Gu (2023). The intrinsic communication in power systems: a new perspective to understand synchronization stability
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers 70(11):4615-4626

citation: Ma, Xin, Li, et al. (2023). Characterizing the Role of Complex Power in Small-Signal Synchronization Stability of Multi-Converter Power Systems
venue: arXiv preprint (v2 2024-02-14); arXiv only - no peer-reviewed version found in Crossref

closest overlap with our work: Operating-point (injection) dependence of each converter's contribution to the network-strength margin, decomposed additively.
exact remaining gap: Preprint. GFL/PLL band only with no SGs. The additive weighted form implies a fixed-sign contribution per injection type, the opposite of contextual sign reversal. No replacement portfolios or line ranking.

citation: Stanojev, Markovic, Aristidou et al. (2023). Improving stability of low-inertia systems using virtual induction machine synchronization for grid-following converters

citation: Yao, Roy, Mathieu (2023). Using demand response to improve power system small-signal stability

closest overlap with our work: Chain-rule eigenvalue sensitivity through algebraic (power-flow) states, i.e., a re-equilibrated sensitivity used to select node-level actions

citation: Zhou, Xin, Wu, et al. (2023). Small-Signal Stability Assessment of Heterogeneous Grid-Following Converter Power Systems Based on Grid Strength Analysis

citation: Zhu, Gu, Li, et al. (2023). Impedance-Based Root-Cause Analysis: Comparative Study of Impedance Models and Calculation of Eigenvalue Sensitivity

citation: Henderson, Egea-Alvarez, Kneuppel, et al. (2024). Grid Strength Impedance Metric: An Alternative to SCR for Evaluating System Strength in Converter Dominated Systems

citation: Huang, Wang, Wang, et al. (2024). Gain and Phase: Decentralized Stability Conditions for Power Electronics-Dominated Power Systems
problem: Scalable, decentralized small-signal stability conditions for heterogeneous multi-converter systems (GFL, GFM, SG).

citation: Liu, Xin, Wu, et al. (2024). Generalized Operational Short-Circuit Ratio for Grid Strength Assessment in Power Systems With High Renewable Penetration
problem: gSCR/CgSCR fail under actual (non-rated) operating conditions of multi-converter systems; need an operating-condition-aware strength index.
method: Multi-time-scale analysis of PLL-dominated dynamics; transformation into simple subsystems; defines gOSCR and CgOSCR using actual terminal voltages and power outputs; usable with black-box converters; modified IEEE 39-bus and a practical wind-rich system.
closest overlap with our work: The gSCR line itself concedes that rated-condition strength indices mis-identify stability once the operating point changes. This supports our claim that static indices are context-blind.
exact remaining gap: Operating-point-aware but still one system index for the PLL band. It is not an intervention sensitivity (no re-equilibrated derivative with respect to replacements or branch admittances), has no SG electromechanical modes, and has no portfolio-conditioned sign or ranking analysis.

citation: Ma, Xin, Wu, et al. (2024). Assessing Small-Signal Grid Strength of 100% Inverter-Based Power Systems
problem: Existing grid strength methods assume SG voltage support and are invalid for 100% IBR systems with GFL and GFM inverters.
method: Multi-inverter small-signal model; grid-strength index with an analytically derived threshold; analytical expression for the impacts of GFL and GFM inverters on the stability boundary; modified IEEE 39-bus.
closest overlap with our work: Same 39-bus test bed; shows the GFL/GFM device mix shifts the stability boundary.
exact remaining gap: No synchronous machines (100% IBR), so no SG-to-GFL replacement or electromechanical-mode tracking; no per-unit marginal effects or sign reversal across portfolios; no line-ranking evaluation.

citation: Yu, Xu, Sun, et al. (2024). Multiple Renewable Short-Circuit Ratio for Assessing Weak System Strength with Inverter-Based Resources
venue: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems 10(6):2271-2282
problem: Identify weak-system status with widely distributed, low-capacity IBRs.
method: Multiple renewable SCR (MRSCR) and its voltage-based critical value (CMRSCR) from a single-infeed equivalent with multiple renewables, linking strength to voltage fluctuation under power variation; implemented in Chinese engineering software.
closest overlap with our work: Utility-grade SCR-family weakness index; the class of static metric our results challenge for small-signal decisions.
exact remaining gap: Static voltage-based index. It does not address small-signal eigenvalues, portfolio-conditioned sign of replacement effects, or line ranking against finite reinforcements.

citation: Chu, Teng (2025). Coordinated planning for stability enhancement in high IBR-penetrated systems
problem: Co-planning synchronous condensers and GFM IBRs for system strength and short-circuit current
method: Analytically derived system-strength and SCC constraints, linearized via data-driven approach, embedded in planning optimization
closest overlap with our work: Stability-constrained planning in IBR-rich transmission systems
exact remaining gap: Strength-type (static) constraints; resources are SCs/GFM only, no transmission-line decisions; no eigenvalue total sensitivity or validation of rankings against finite dynamic outcomes

citation: Lamrani, Prevost, Cardozo, et al. (2025). Frequency-Averaged Grid Impedance Metric for Identifying Weakest Buses in Power Electronics-Dominated Systems
problem: Identify weakest buses (risk of inverter interaction) in PEIR-dominated systems; SCR-derived metrics are inadequate.
method: Frequency Averaged Grid Impedance (FAGI) metric capturing PEIR under various control schemes, compared with ESCR as implemented in RTE's operational tool; 4-VSC system; dynamic simulations used to check each metric's bus ranking.
closest overlap with our work: Scores bus rankings from static strength metrics against dynamic ground truth and finds ESCR-derived rankings unreliable, which parallels our static-metric baseline comparison.
exact remaining gap: Small 4-VSC system and bus ranking only. No SGs, no replacement portfolios or sign reversal, no line-reinforcement ranking. The fixed-ranking issue shown concerns ESCR-vs-dynamics disagreement, not ranking failure across portfolio contexts.

citation: Oduor, Munda, Akumu et al. (2025). Optimization of topological reconfiguration by transmission line switching for damping inter-area oscillations in power systems
problem: Line switching for voltage control without triggering interarea oscillatory instability
method: Quadratic eigenvalue analysis; multi-objective particle swarm optimization selecting lines to switch off; IEEE 30-, 39- and 68-bus
closest overlap with our work: IEEE 39-bus topology changes shown to both help and harm small-signal stability
exact remaining gap: Metaheuristic search, no sensitivity-based ranking; no GFL replacement portfolios; no comparison with static topology metrics

citation: Xin, Liu, Chen, et al. (2025). How Many Grid-Forming Converters Do We Need? A Perspective From Small Signal Stability and Power Grid Strength
problem: Which voltage-source behaviour (GFL with voltage control vs GFM) strengthens the grid in small-signal terms, and how many/where GFM units are needed.
method: Small-signal analysis via equivalent power grid strength (gSCR-type); effect of the GFM:GFL capacity ratio on the stability margin; configuration guidelines; high-fidelity simulations.
closest overlap with our work: Poses a portfolio-design question (how many and where to convert) and answers it through grid strength.
exact remaining gap: Treats GFM addition as monotonically strengthening and GFL as not providing effective voltage support. It does not study SG-to-GFL replacements in the 0.1-2 Hz electromechanical band, sign reversal of the same replacement across (nested) portfolios, or how often a fixed ranking fails.

citation: Bacic, Niehues, Bottcher, et al. (2026). A graph theoretic view on small signal stability of inverter-based power grids
problem: Necessary and sufficient small-signal stability conditions for lossless inverter-based grids and decentralized certificates.
method: Stability shown equivalent to positive definiteness of a single matrix combining topology, operating point (voltages, angle differences) and droop gains; augmented cone graphs; decentralized criteria and their conservatism; IEEE 9-, 30-, 118-bus.
closest overlap with our work: Graph-spectral small-signal condition with operating-point-dependent edge weights (topic 11).
exact remaining gap: Droop-controlled grid-forming inverters only, lossless, and negative edge weights excluded (cos(theta_ij)>0). No GFL/SG, no replacement portfolios, no sign reversal, no line ranking vs finite interventions.

citation: Desai, Stanojev, Muntwiler et al. (2026). Effect of dispatch decisions on small-signal stability of converter-dominated power systems
problem: How active/reactive dispatch and voltage setpoints of GFL/GFM converters shape small-signal stable operating regions
method: Repeated power-flow solution, linearization and eigenvalue computation over dispatch grids (no analytic sensitivity); GFL with PLL, GFM droop, 8th-order SGs; 3-bus and IEEE 39-bus with replaced SGs
closest overlap with our work: IEEE 39-bus with converters replacing SGs; shows opposite dispatch preferences for GFL vs GFM (converter-type-dependent effects) on re-solved equilibria
exact remaining gap: Varies dispatch, not branch parameters or replacement sets; no sensitivity-based ranking, no fixed-ranking failure analysis, no topology interventions

citation: Joswig-Jones, Dong, Tan et al. (2026). Sensitivity-based system strength assessment: mapping power flow and network topology perturbations to system eigenvalues
venue: arXiv preprint (submitted to IEEE Transactions on Power Systems; not peer reviewed)
problem: System-strength metrics for IBR-rich grids based on eigenvalue sensitivities to power injections, voltages and line admittances
method: Impedance-based eigenvalue sensitivity with chain rule through power-flow sensitivities (partitioned Jacobians), i.e., operating-point changes included; line susceptance sensitivities (R/X fixed); modified IEEE 14-bus (GFL) and 118-bus (SG+GFL+GFM); validated against perturbed eigenvalues (small errors) and time-domain line-trip cases; compared qualitatively with impedance margin ratio
closest overlap with our work: Closest methodological overlap: total (power-flow-coupled) eigenvalue sensitivity to line admittances in IBR systems, used to flag critical lines
exact remaining gap: No rank-correlation of branch sensitivities against finite re-solved reinforcements; no comparison with SCR/gSCR/Fiedler/Kirchhoff; no nested replacement portfolios or context-dependent sign reversal study; preprint only

citation: Zhang, Chen, Chen et al. (2026). Small-signal stability and inertia constrained optimal configuration method of grid-forming energy storage systems
problem: Optimal placement and capacity of GFM energy storage under small-signal stability and inertia constraints
method: Small-signal model of multi-converter system; stability criteria vs GFM ESS placement/capacity; mixed-integer program with relaxed eigenvalue constraints; two-layer iterative algorithm
closest overlap with our work: Same IEEE 39-bus; joint (portfolio-level) siting with eigenvalue constraints rather than a fixed node ranking
exact remaining gap: Adds GFM ESS rather than replacing SGs with GFL; abstract reports no marginal-effect sign reversal, no submodularity analysis, no AVR/Q-V gain dependence study (only abstract verified)

citation: Lamrani, Cardozo, Prevost et al. (2027). Placing grid-forming controlled converters to enhance power system small-signal stability
problem: Placement of GFM-controlled converters for small-signal stability of transmission grids
method: Journal abstract not accessible; the first author's PhD thesis (doi 10.70675/2e96c2d1zb44az4511z91fazef7a34c9c2d7) describes an iterative placement methodology using a weakest-point indicator (FAGI) and a stability indicator (MnPI) based on impedance models, and finds the stabilizing effect varies with GFM control type
closest overlap with our work: Recent iterative (sequential) GFM placement for small-signal stability
exact remaining gap: Content of journal version not verified; no evidence found of SG->GFL replacement sign reversal, submodularity test, or fixed-ranking evaluation
